_comment: Reviewer judgments for docs/QUOTE_TRANSLATION_AUDIT.md, one entry per quotation per locale. The exact quotation and byline are NOT stored here — scripts/build-quote-audit.mjs reads them from apps/web/src/data/quotes.ts so the table cannot drift from the runtime data — and the wrapping / RTL columns come from docs/quote-render-audit.json, written by scripts/qa-quote-render.mjs from the rendered screen. What IS here is the reading: a back-translation, the grammar and naturalness judgment, the punctuation check, the status, the correction made, and what a native speaker still has to confirm. Reviewed 12 September 2026 by the model that wrote the translations; NATIVE-SPEAKER REVIEW REQUIRED marks the rows where that is not enough.

en.bt: Dream big. Even if it shatters, the pieces will be big.
en.attribution: Author unknown — the plain English byline for an unattributed line.

ko.grammar: Canonical wording as specified; 해라체 imperative, natural.
ko.punct: Two sentences, full stops, as specified.

ja.bt: Hold your dream big. Even if it shatters, its fragments are big.
ja.grammar: 持て is the plain imperative the line is usually quoted with in Japanese; かけら keeps the fragment image.

zh-CN.bt: Dreams should be grand. Even if shattered, the fragments are big.
zh-CN.grammar: 梦想要远大 is the set phrase; 碎片也是大的 keeps the pieces literal rather than abstract.
zh-CN.correction: First draft 要有大梦想。即使梦碎了，碎片也依然很大。 read as a literal gloss; replaced with the set phrase 梦想要远大 and a plainer second clause.
zh-CN.attribution: 作者不详 — standard (佚名 would read as a pen name).

es.bt: Dream big. Even if it breaks, the pieces will be big.
es.grammar: Sueña en grande is idiomatic; subjunctive after aunque; pedazos for broken pieces.

fr.bt: Dream big. Even if it breaks, the pieces will stay big.
fr.grammar: Rêve en grand is idiomatic; typographic apostrophe in s’il.

de.bt: Dream big. Even if the dream breaks, the pieces stay big.
de.grammar: Träume groß is the usual rendering; der Traum repeated so zerbricht has an unambiguous subject.

pt-BR.bt: Dream big. Even if the dream breaks, the pieces will be big.
pt-BR.grammar: Brazilian imperative sonhe; subjunctive after mesmo que.

vi.bt: Dream really big. Even if the dream breaks, the broken pieces are still big.
vi.grammar: Hãy + verb imperative; mảnh vỡ keeps the fragment image. Register plausible; a native reader should confirm mảnh vỡ vẫn lớn reads as encouragement rather than as a physical description.
vi.punct: Two sentences, full stops; diacritics complete.
vi.review: Confirm register of the second clause (mảnh vỡ vẫn lớn) for a motivational line.
vi.attribution: Khuyết danh — the standard Vietnamese label for an unattributed text.

th.bt: Dream big; even if the dream shatters, its fragments are still big.
th.grammar: จง gives the exhortative register a quoted maxim takes; แตกสลาย = shatter; เศษ = fragments.
th.punct: Thai uses spaces between clauses and no full stop, as here.
th.review: Confirm เศษของมัน over เศษเสี้ยว for the fragment image, and the จง register.
th.attribution: ไม่ทราบผู้แต่ง — ‘author not known’.

ar.bt: Dream big dreams; for even if they shatter, their fragments remain big.
ar.grammar: Imperative احلم with cognate object; فحتى إن introduces the concession; شظايا = fragments.
ar.punct: Arabic comma ،; final full stop; shadda on تحطّمت.
ar.review: Confirm شظايا (shards) over قطع (pieces) for the intended image, and MSA register.
ar.attribution: قائل مجهول — ‘unknown sayer’, used for sayings rather than مؤلف (a book’s author).

bn.bt: See big dreams. Even if they break, their pieces remain big.
bn.grammar: দেখো familiar imperative, the register of a maxim; টুকরোগুলো = the pieces.
bn.review: Confirm বড়ই থাকে (remain big indeed) reads naturally; alternative বড়ই হয়.

cs.bt: Dream big. Even if the dream breaks, big pieces remain of it.
cs.grammar: Sni ve velkém is idiomatic Czech; po něm refers to the dream.

el.bt: Have big dreams. Even if they break, their pieces stay big.
el.grammar: Κάνε μεγάλα όνειρα is the natural Greek; plural carried through.
el.punct: Two sentences, full stops; accents complete.

fil.bt: Dream big. Even if it breaks, the pieces are still big.
fil.grammar: Mangarap nang malaki idiomatic; mabasag = get broken (glass-like), fits the image.
fil.review: Confirm mabasag over masira for a dream; confirm malalaki pa rin ang mga piraso word order.

hi.bt: See big dreams. Even if they break, their pieces are also big.
hi.grammar: देखो familiar imperative; टूट भी जाएँ subjunctive concession; टुकड़े = pieces.
hi.punct: Devanagari danda ।; nukta on ज़ not needed here.
hi.review: Confirm the concessive तो … भी construction reads as a maxim rather than as prose.

hu.bt: Dream big! Even if it breaks, its pieces stay big.
hu.grammar: Álmodj nagyot! is the idiom; exclamation mark is normal for a Hungarian imperative.
hu.punct: Imperative with !, then a full stop.

id.bt: Dream big. Even if it breaks, its pieces stay big.
id.grammar: Bermimpilah yang besar is idiomatic; kepingan = fragments.

it.bt: Dream big. Even if the dream breaks, the pieces remain big.
it.grammar: Sogna in grande is the idiom; si spezza for break.

kk.bt: May your dream be big. Even if it collapses, its shards will be big.
kk.grammar: Арманың үлкен болсын is the natural optative; сынықтары = its shards.
kk.punct: Two sentences, full stops; Cyrillic Kazakh letters ң, ү, і present.
kk.correction: First draft Үлкен арман арманда repeated the cognate (арман/арманда, ‘dream a dream’), which reads as a translation; replaced with the optative Арманың үлкен болсын.
kk.review: Native confirmation of сынықтары (shards) versus бөлшектері (pieces) is advisable; grammar and meaning are sound.

ky.bt: May your dream be big. Even if it shatters, its shards will be big.
ky.grammar: Кыялың чоң болсун optative, parallel to Kazakh; талкаланса = if it shatters.
ky.punct: Two sentences, full stops; Kyrgyz ң, ү present.
ky.correction: First draft Чоң кыялдан (‘dream big’ as a bare imperative) is unidiomatic; replaced with the optative Кыялың чоң болсун.
ky.review: Native confirmation of сыныктары advisable; grammar and meaning are sound.

mn.bt: Dream big. Even if it shatters, its fragments are big.
mn.grammar: Том мөрөөд imperative; хэлтэрхий = fragments; нь marks the possessed subject.
mn.correction: First draft Хэдий хагарсан ч … том хэвээр байна was wordy (‘however much it broke, still remains big’); shortened to Хагарсан ч хэлтэрхий нь том байна.
mn.review: Native confirmation of хэлтэрхий for the image; grammar and meaning are sound.

nl.bt: Dream big. Even if the dream breaks, the pieces stay big.
nl.grammar: Droom groot is idiomatic; de droom repeated for a clear subject.

pl.bt: Have great dreams. Even if they shatter, their pieces will remain great.
pl.grammar: Miej wielkie marzenia is the idiom (dreams are plural in Polish usage); wielkie carries both ‘big’ and ‘great’.

ro.bt: Dream grandly. Even if the dream breaks, the pieces remain big.
ro.grammar: Visează măreț idiomatic; se sparge for break.
ro.punct: Two sentences, full stops; ș/ț with comma-below.

ru.bt: Dream big. Even if the dream shatters, its shards will be big.
ru.grammar: Мечтай по-крупному is the idiom; осколки = shards, the standard rendering of this line in Russian.
ru.punct: Two sentences, full stops; ё written.

sv.bt: Dream big. Even if the dream breaks, the pieces become big.
sv.grammar: Dröm stort idiomatic; går sönder = breaks.

ta.bt: Dream big. Even if it breaks, its pieces will still be big.
ta.grammar: Polite plural imperative காணுங்கள்; துண்டுகள் = pieces; -ஆகவே இருக்கும் = will indeed remain.
ta.punct: Two sentences, full stops; no glyph gaps.
ta.review: Confirm the polite imperative is right for a maxim and that the second sentence is not over-long in Tamil.

te.bt: Dream big dreams. Even if they break, those pieces will also be big.
te.grammar: కనండి polite imperative; పగిలినా concessive; ముక్కలు = pieces.
te.review: Confirm పెద్దవిగానే (as indeed big) for register.

tr.bt: Set big dreams. Even if it breaks, its pieces are big.
tr.grammar: Büyük hayaller kur is the idiom; kırılsa bile concession.

uk.bt: Dream big. Even if the dream shatters, its shards will be big.
uk.punct: Two sentences, full stops; typographic apostrophe in розіб’ється.

uz.bt: Dream a big dream. Even if it breaks, its pieces will be big.
uz.grammar: Katta orzu qil imperative; parchalari = its pieces; Latin Uzbek with ‘ in bo‘ladi.
uz.punct: Two sentences, full stops; Uzbek ‘ (U+2018) as the standard apostrophe.
uz.review: Confirm sinsa (breaks) versus buzilsa for a dream.

en.bt: When a stone lies in the road, the weak call it a stumbling block; the strong call it a stepping stone.
en.grammar: The established English pairing stumbling block / stepping stone; parallel clauses.
en.punct: Semicolon between the two parallel clauses.

ko.grammar: Canonical wording as specified; 걸림돌/디딤돌 is the native idiom pair.
ko.punct: Comma after the first clause, full stop, as specified.
ko.attribution: 토머스 칼라일 — the standard Korean transcription.

ja.bt: When a stone appears while walking a road, the weak call it a ‘stone of stumbling’ and the strong call it a ‘stepping stone’.
ja.grammar: つまずきの石 / 踏み石 is the natural Japanese pair; 「」quote the two names as names.
ja.punct: Japanese 、and 。; corner brackets around the two terms.
ja.attribution: トーマス・カーライル — standard katakana.

zh-CN.bt: Meeting a stone on the road, the weak call it a stumbling stone; the strong call it a stepping stone.
zh-CN.grammar: 绊脚石 / 垫脚石 is the exact Chinese idiom pair.

es.bt: When a stone appears in the road, the weak one calls it an obstacle and the strong one calls it a step.
es.grammar: obstáculo / escalón is the natural Spanish contrast; la llama repeated for parallelism.
es.punct: One sentence, comma after the subordinate clause.
es.correction: First draft used tropiezo / peldaño; tropiezo as a bare noun for the stone is stilted. Replaced with obstáculo / escalón.

fr.bt: When a stone stands in the way, the weak calls it an obstacle and the strong, a stepping stone.
fr.grammar: obstacle / marchepied is the natural French pair; the elided second verb (et le fort, un marchepied) is standard.
fr.punct: Typographic apostrophes; comma marking the ellipsis.

de.bt: If a stone lies in the way, the weak calls it a stumbling stone and the strong a stepping stone.
de.grammar: Stolperstein / Trittstein is the exact German idiom pair.
de.punct: One sentence, comma after the conditional clause.

pt-BR.bt: When a stone appears in the way, the weak calls it an obstacle and the strong calls it a step.
pt-BR.grammar: obstáculo / degrau; a chama de is the Brazilian construction.
pt-BR.correction: First draft tropeço / degrau; tropeço reads as ‘a stumble’, not the stone. Replaced with obstáculo.

vi.bt: On meeting a stone on the road, the weak call it a road-blocking stone, while the strong call it a springboard.
vi.grammar: đá cản đường (road-blocking stone) against bàn đạp (stepping board / springboard) keeps the contrast; kẻ yếu / người mạnh is the usual pairing.
vi.review: Confirm bàn đạp is the natural counterpart to đá cản đường in this register.

th.bt: When one meets a stone blocking the way, the weak person calls it an obstacle, but the strong person calls it a stair.
th.grammar: อุปสรรค / บันได is the natural Thai contrast; ขวางทาง = blocking the way.
th.punct: Thai clause spacing, no full stop.
th.review: Confirm บันได (stair) over ขั้นบันได (step) for the image.
th.attribution: โทมัส คาร์ไลล์ — the Thai spelling used in reference works.

ar.bt: When a stone blocks your path, the weak calls it a stumble, and the strong calls it a step he climbs on.
ar.grammar: عثرة (stumble/obstacle) against درجة يصعد عليها (a step one climbs) keeps the contrast explicit; حجرٌ with tanwin as indefinite subject.
ar.punct: Arabic commas ،; final full stop; tanwin and fatha on درجةً.
ar.review: Confirm عثرة is the idiomatic counterpart to حجر عثرة here, and the relative clause يصعد عليها is not heavy.

bn.bt: If a stone lies on the path, the weak calls it an obstacle, and the strong calls it a step of a staircase.
bn.grammar: বাধা / সিঁড়ির ধাপ; দুর্বল / সবল pairing.
bn.review: Confirm সিঁড়ির ধাপ over পাদানি for ‘stepping stone’.

cs.bt: When a stone appears on the path, the weak calls it a stone of injury and the strong a springboard stone.
cs.grammar: kámen úrazu (stumbling block) / odrazový kámen (stepping stone) are the Czech idioms.

el.bt: When a stone is found in the road, the weak calls it an obstacle and the strong a step.
el.grammar: εμπόδιο / σκαλοπάτι is the natural Greek contrast.

fil.bt: When a stone blocks the road, the weak calls it a hindrance and the strong a step.
fil.grammar: hadlang / baitang; ng mahina / ng malakas as agents.
fil.review: Confirm the compressed second half (tinatawag itong hadlang ng mahina at baitang ng malakas) is not ambiguous in Filipino.

hi.bt: If a stone comes in the way, the weak calls it a stumble, and the strong calls it a ladder.
hi.grammar: ठोकर (a stumble; also the stone one trips on) / सीढ़ी (step, ladder) is a natural Hindi contrast.
hi.punct: Danda ।; nukta in कमज़ोर and मज़बूत.
hi.review: Confirm ठोकर reads as the stone rather than only the act of tripping.

hu.bt: If a stone gets in the way, the weak calls it an obstacle, the strong a stair step.
hu.correction: First draft botlásnak (‘a stumble’) named the act, not the stone; replaced with akadálynak.

id.bt: When a stone blocks the road, the weak person calls it a stumbling stone, the strong person calls it a stepping stone.
id.grammar: batu sandungan / batu pijakan are the Indonesian idioms.
id.correction: First draft sandungan / pijakan dropped batu; the idioms are batu sandungan and batu pijakan.

it.bt: When a stone is on the path, the weak calls it an obstacle and the strong a step.
it.grammar: ostacolo / gradino; elided second verb is standard.
it.correction: First draft inciampo / gradino; inciampo alone is ‘a trip’. Replaced with un ostacolo.

kk.bt: If a stone is met on the road, the weak calls it an obstacle, the strong calls it a step.
kk.review: Confirm баспалдақ (staircase/step) is the natural counterpart to кедергі.
kk.attribution: Томас Карлейль — the Cyrillic form shared with Russian.

ky.bt: If a stone is met on the road, the weak calls it an obstacle, the strong calls it a step.

mn.bt: If a stone is met on the road, the weak person calls it an obstacle, the strong person calls it a step.
mn.review: Confirm гишгүүр for ‘stepping stone’ and сул дорой for ‘the weak’.

nl.bt: If a stone lies on the road, the weak calls it a stumbling block and the strong a step-up.
nl.grammar: struikelblok / opstapje are the Dutch idioms.

pl.bt: When a stone appears on the road, the weak calls it an obstacle, and the strong — a step.
pl.grammar: przeszkodą / stopniem; em dash for the elided verb is standard Polish.

ro.bt: When a stone appears in the road, the weak calls it a hindrance, and the strong calls it a step.
ro.grammar: piedică / treaptă; cel slab / cel puternic.

ru.bt: When a stone is met on the way, the weak calls it a barrier, and the strong — a step.
ru.grammar: преграда / ступень; em dash for the elided verb is standard Russian.

sv.bt: When a stone lies on the road, the weak calls it a stumbling block and the strong a stair step.
sv.grammar: stötesten / trappsteg are the Swedish idioms.

ta.bt: If a stone gets in the way on the road, the weak person calls it an obstacle-stone; the strong person calls it a step-stone.
ta.grammar: தடைக்கல் / படிக்கல் compound the stone into both names, mirroring 걸림돌/디딤돌.
ta.review: Confirm the coined compounds தடைக்கல் / படிக்கல் read naturally rather than as calques.

te.bt: If a stone comes in the way, the weak calls it an obstructing stone; the strong calls it a step.
te.review: Confirm అడ్డురాయి is idiomatic for ‘stumbling block’.

tr.bt: When a stone appears in the road, the weak calls it an obstacle; the strong, a step.
tr.grammar: engel / basamak; güçlü ise for the contrast.

uk.bt: When a stone is met on the way, the weak calls it an obstacle, and the strong — a step.
uk.grammar: перешкода / сходинка; dash for the elided verb.

uz.bt: If a stone is met on the road, the weak calls it an obstacle, while the strong calls it a staircase.
uz.grammar: to‘siq / zinapoya; esa for the contrast.
uz.review: Confirm zinapoya (staircase) over zina/pog‘ona (step) for the image.
